From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Holden Biotech — request for bespoke availability exemption and operational asks

Team,

Summary: Holden Biotech (clinical triage product) is asking for a bespoke availability/latency commitment for a pilot that, if successful, will convert to a 12-month reserved contract. They need a temporary carveout for a 99.95% availability commitment and an operational escalation path for sub-200ms p95 for a small set of routes.

Key asks from Holden (see attached):
- 99.95% availability for the critical /triage endpoint (they will route ~120TPS).
- p95 latency target <= 200ms for production requests during business hours (PST).
- A named escalation contact and 15-minute ACK during critical incidents.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence and audit log retention 180 days.

Attachments: holden_mop_v1.pdf (customer MOP), edge-availability-matrix.xlsx (their traffic pattern and sequence lengths).

What I need from this thread:
1) Product: feasibility + recommended fallback model variant and cache strategy.
2) Infra/ops: brief runbook & run-rate cost delta for keeping dedicated warm capacity.
3) Commercial: provisional approval route (who signs off on a temporary SLA carveout while legal finalizes terms).

Options I propose:
A) Approve short-term carveout (30 days) tied to a 12-month reserved commit and 25% premium on token pricing.
B) Offer a staged SLO: 99.9% + product-level mitigations now, full 99.95% post-reserved-provisioning.

Timeline: Holden expects a Go/No-Go by EOD Tue 4/20; procurement wants language to include in their PO.

Can Marcus/Marissa/Monica weigh in on feasibility and a recommended approval path? If we can agree on an interim option I will present it back to Holden and loop Legal/Finance.

Thanks,
Sean

Sean —

Thanks for the summary. High-level thoughts: we can probably support a temporary carveout, but there are non-trivial product and ops implications. A few clarifying Qs before I greenlight anything: 

- Is the 120TPS steady or bursty (they included a histogram in the matrix but I want p95/p99 burst characteristics)?
- Which model(s) do they plan to run in prod? If it's a 13B with kv-cache heavy usage, the p95 delta is different than for a quantized 7B.
- Are they open to an application-level mitigation (prefix caching, responses with progressive fallback to smaller model) if we can't meet 200ms p95 for all requests?

Operational constraints:
- Dedicated warm capacity to guarantee 200ms p95 for 120TPS will require reserving an additional instance pool in the same region. I'll ask infra for a rough cost delta; rough estimate: +30-45% on top of standard reserved pricing until we can tune batching and caching.
- Escalation: we can provide a named on-call and a 15-minute ACK during business hours; 24/7 would be a different tier.

Commercially, I can approve a 30-day interim carveout if we get: 1) a signed commercial intent (deal_id above) for 12 months and 2) an agreement to accept staged fallback policies we define. Anything more permanent needs Legal/Finance sign-off.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Marcus: produce a one-page runbook and a cost delta number by EOD Mon 4/19.
2) Marissa: confirm model compatibility and whether prefix caching + fallback can keep user-visible latency within expectations.
3) Sean: relay these asks to Holden and get confirmation on committed model + intent to sign.

I'll be available to join a call with Holden tomorrow if needed.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Internal commitments:

- Marissa: validate model routing and fallback options; specify what we'll degrade to if we detect sustained P95 violations.
- Monica: provisional commercial approval for a 30-day carveout tied to a 12-month reserved commitment; Legal/Finance to draft final terms.

Proposed interim carveout (draft summary we can include in PO):
"Redwood will provide a temporary availability commitment of 99.95% to the /triage endpoint for a 30-day pilot period starting on the signed PO date. Redwood will assign a named escalation contact with 15-minute ACK during business hours (PST). If Redwood cannot meet the 200ms p95 target consistently, Redwood will trigger the pre-agreed fallback policy (smaller model or cached responses) and provide credit remedies consistent with company policy. This interim carveout is contingent on Holden signing a 12-month reserved capacity agreement within 30 days of PO execution."

Action items for Holden: please confirm acceptance of the draft language above and confirm the PO start date you plan to use. If ok, I'll ask Legal to draft the formal carveout appendix and route a DocuSign.
